title: Publisher dealflow onboarding brief + legal Q&A (draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc is a short-form onboarding brief for publisher / channel partners who will list Redwood Inference on cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). It combines: 1) the operational checklist we require to accept a publisher listing into our dealflow pipeline, 2) a set of copy variants for marketplace product pages (short + long descriptions, bullets), and 3) a legal + compliance Q&A we run with partners early in the process.

Audience
- Partner onboarding managers
- Marketplace ops and listing owners
- Solutions and legal leads for publisher partners
- GTM PMs preparing marketplace rollout assets

High-level objectives
- Reduce back-and-forth by standardizing the initial submission bundle (what partners must send for us to accept into internal review)
- Provide copy variants that are pre-approved for common marketplaces to speed creative turnaround
- Surface legal/policy gaps early so engineering and security teams can scope integration work quickly

Quick summary of pipeline steps (publisher dealflow)
1) Intake: partner fills initial questionnaire and uploads the submission bundle (see required artifacts).
2) Vet: GTM reviews copy, pricing model, and initial security attestation. If acceptable, route to integration engineering for technical assessment.
3) Integrate: engineering runs smoke test, IAM review, and billing SKU mapping.
4) Certify: legal and compliance sign off, final pricing approved.
5) Publish: marketplace listing submitted, partner onboarding call scheduled, marketing assets shared.

Required submission bundle (minimum to accept into dealflow)
- Marketplace listing brief (doc) with suggested product title, 1-sentence tagline, 2–3 short bullets, long description (300–600 characters), and 3 feature bullets mapped to customer outcomes.
- Pricing proposal: single-sheet with proposed SKU mapping, unit metrics (per-token/per-request or time-based), and suggested trial/credits.
- Technical checklist completion: partner fills the Technical Preflight form (attached template) including endpoints, auth method, sample request/response, and rate-limit profile.
- Security attestation: completed security questionnaire or SOC/ISO summary + contact for security review.
- Commercial attachments: partner invoice/PO template, tax form (if required), and reseller agreement draft if co-selling.

Marketplace product copy (variants)
Short tagline (for tile)
- Variant A (developer-centric): "High-performance LLM inference — predictable latency, lower unit costs."
- Variant B (product-centric): "Deploy advanced generative features with production SLAs and cost controls."

300–600 char long description (copy bank)
- Variant A: "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first platform for serving large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features quickly with predictable latency, cost-aware controls, and built-in fallbacks for high availability. Includes dashboards, routing policies, and model optimization tooling for production workloads."
- Variant B: "A unified inference runtime that makes LLMs practical at scale. Reduce token costs with workload-aware batching and KV caching, maintain SLAs with multi-tier routing, and deploy into VPCs for regulated workloads. Ideal for product teams building chat, summarization, and embeddings at scale."

Feature bullets (3)
- Production performance: "Optimized runtime with batching and quantization recommendations to lower per-token cost without degrading quality."
- Deployment options: "Hosted API, reserved dedicated capacity, or private VPC/on-prem installs with KMS integration."
- Observable economics: "Per-route token cost breakdowns, latency histograms, and regression alerts tied to eval suites."

Copy guidance & gating rules
- Keep marketplace tile taglines < 60 characters.
- Long descriptions should avoid platform-specific claims (e.g., "AWS-exclusive") unless partner has channel exclusivity confirmed in writing.
- Don’t reference pricing tiers directly in the long description. Pricing goes into the pricing proposal only.
- Use plain-English benefit statements rather than deep implementation detail.

Acceptance checklist for internal review (GTM + Legal + Eng)
- Copy sanity: title/tagline approved, description matches approved feature bullets.
- Pricing sanity: per-SKU unit mechanics clear, trial credits defined.
- Security check: SOC/ISO summary on file or passing security questionnaire.
- Integration readiness: sample API keys, test account, and smoke test run results present.
- Billing readiness: SKU codes and invoicing contact confirmed.

Technical preflight highlights (what Eng looks for)
- Auth and keys: supported auth method (API key, marketplace IAM token), rotation policy, and whom to contact for ephemeral test keys.
- Endpoint and SLA: region(s), expected p95 latency on test inputs, and retry/backoff semantics.
- Data handling: whether partner sends PII, whether requests are logged for debugging, and retention policy.
- Fall-back model plan: what we do if primary model is unavailable (downgrade to smaller model, regional fallback).

Legal & compliance starter Q&A (things to confirm up-front)
Q: Who is the data controller for customer inputs processed through the marketplace listing?
A: Default: the partner is the controller for customer data submitted to their integration; Redwood acts as processor for hosted endpoints. Any deviation requires legal review and contract language.

Q: Do we need a separate Data Processing Agreement (DPA) for this publisher listing?
A: If the partner or customers are in regulated industries (finance/healthcare) or we will store logs beyond 30 days, yes. Flag early.

Q: Are there export control or cryptography disclosures required by the cloud marketplace?
A: Usually marketplaces require basic export-control declarations. If model weights or custom binaries are transferred, route to Security for an export assessment.

Q: Can partner claim full-stack ownership for a "private deployment" SKU?
A: Not without a separate Private Deployment contract amendment. Marketplace copy must not promise unattended on-prem installs without a cleared SOW.

Operational notes / timeline expectations
- Standard time-to-publish after complete bundle: 3–5 weeks (avg). Typical blockers: security questionnaire responses, unresolved pricing/legal language, or missing test credentials.
- Fast-track path: if partner provides SOC2 and a signed reseller addendum, target 10 business days.

Risks we watch for
- Overbroad claims in copy about model capabilities (hallucination/accuracy guarantees). We push neutral benefit statements and link to evaluation notes.
- Hidden data retention that conflicts with partner/regulator expectations.
- Unclear SKU mechanics that require engineering to implement two different billing meters.

Next actions for partner intake owner (template)
1) Send this brief + submission bundle checklist to partner.
2) Request the Technical Preflight form (attached) + security artifacts.
3) Assign internal reviewers: one GTM, one Eng, one Security, one Legal.
4) Kickoff meeting within 5 business days of bundle receipt; aim to triage blockers in the first call.

Appendix: sample privacy blurb for listing (editable)
"Requests are routed to Redwood Inference for processing. We retain logs for up to 30 days for operational debugging; customers can opt into longer retention if explicitly contracted. For regulated workloads, choose our Private deployment option to keep data inside your VPC and under your key management."

Notes/TODO (work-in-progress)
- Need final approved long-description language for each cloud marketplace to account for character limits and formatting.
- Confirm whether marketplaces accept markdown or plain text for feature bullets — impacts copy styling.
- Update pricing template to include marketplace commission model for AWS/Azure/GCP (currently a placeholder).

Owner & contacts

- Security review contact: Dylan Ortiz — dylan@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: Esha Patel — esha@redwood.ai

End of brief
